en.title: Coyote vs. Acme's Box Office Victory Proves Looney Tunes Deserve Better
en.summary: Against all odds, **Coyote vs. Acme** has triumphed at the box office, proving that audiences are hungry for well-executed Looney Tunes content. This unexpected success story shines a spotlight on the franchise's enduring appeal.
en.body:
In a move that defied industry expectations and silenced critics who predicted its demise, **Coyote vs. Acme** has roared to success in its opening weekend. Projected to earn between $11 and $14 million, the live-action/animated hybrid film instead pulled in a remarkable $15.9 million domestically and nearly $24 million worldwide. This triumph is even more impressive considering **Ketchup Entertainment**'s modest marketing budget of approximately $10 million, a fraction of the film's $70 million production cost. The film's performance is a clear victory lap for **Looney Tunes** fans and a testament to the enduring power of classic animation.

This success is particularly resonant given the film's tumultuous journey, having been reportedly shelved by **Warner Bros. Discovery** CEO **David Zaslav** for a tax write-off. **Coyote vs. Acme** has now outgrossed the opening weekends of four other Warner Bros. releases this year, including **Evil Dead Rise** and **The Mummy**, all without the backing of a major studio's full marketing apparatus. The film's director, **Dave Green**, alongside stars **Will Forte**, **Lana Condor**, and **John Cena**, have delivered a project that captures the clever humor and over-the-top absurdity that has defined the **Looney Tunes** for generations.

## A Mirror to Our Own Struggles

The critical reception has been equally enthusiastic, with praise for its ability to make **Wile E. Coyote** an aspirational figure. Reviewers noted the film's success in portraying him as a mirror to our own Sisyphean struggles, without sacrificing his anarchic spirit. He remains obsessive, self-destructive, and blind to the friendships that sustain him, yet his determination in the face of endless failure resonates deeply. "He is a bit of a sadist, obsessive to the point of self-destructive, deceptive towards his allies, and blind to the friendships that actually sustain him," noted one review, "his characterization here as a messy little bitch is just that sharp."

## What Fans Are Saying

Fans have responded overwhelmingly positively, expressing relief and joy that a project with such potential wasn't permanently lost. The film's ability to capture the "perfectly silly" essence of the **Looney Tunes** has been a major talking point. For years, the beloved characters have been largely neglected or underserved in feature films, making **Coyote vs. Acme** feel like a much-needed breath of fresh air. The movie is seen not just as a win for **Ketchup Entertainment**, but for anyone who appreciates the clever, timeless humor of **Bugs Bunny**, **Daffy Duck**, and their animated cohorts.

## What's Next

With a confirmed release date of August 28, 2026, **Coyote vs. Acme** has finally arrived in theaters, proving its mettle. The film's strong performance suggests a potential shift in how **Warner Bros. Discovery** views its extensive animation library, potentially paving the way for more classic characters to receive similar treatment.

content_raw: There are several ways to look at the Coyote vs. Acme opening this past weekend. The first is that the movie performed well past expectations and deserves a carrot in addition to a well-timed “what’s up doc?” for its effort. This picture was, after all, generally projected to earn between $11 and $14 million by industry prognosticators, yet wound up grossing $15.9 million in the U.S. and nearly $24 million worldwide in its opening weekend. That’s incredibly strong when you realize Ketchup Entertainment only spent about $10 million marketing it, a pittance compared to its estimated $70 million budget. It’s also nearly double Ridley Scott’s Dog Soldiers , which opened to $8 million in North America. This is definitely a victory lap for Ketchup, Looney Tunes fans, and just lovers of cinema in general. The movie Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav previously patted himself on the back as taking “ courage ” to bury for a tax write-off just outgrossed the debuts of four WB movies this year: Evil Dead Burn , T hey Will Kill You , The Bride! , and Lee Cronin’s The Mummy . And it did this without a major studio’s marketing apparatus (and budget) behind it. Nonetheless, the news is still a little bittersweet when coupled with the fact it’s still “merely” the third best Looney Tunes feature film debut, opening well behind Space Jam: A New Legacy when it launched with $31 million in July 2021 despite the world still being in the throes of the pandemic, and WB in the midst of a misjudged decision to release its entire 2021 slate day-and-date in theaters and on HBO Max. It is also below the first Space Jam , which opened to $27.5 million way back in 1996, an astounding $58.5 million in 2026 dollars. It’s likewise beneath the adjusted opening of 1988’s seminal Who Framed Roger Rabbit and its $31.6 million gross when shifted for inflation. This is understandable. Ketchup Entertainment is an independent distributor and they picked up Coyote vs. Acme only after the studio whose logo is synonymous with Looney Tunes begrudgingly shopped the title following turbulent online backlash against the shelving of yet another nearly finished film—this one now generally recognized as a good time with Wile E. Coyote, the Road Runner, and the rest of the Looney Tunes gang. Its qualified success, then, is yet one final, reassuring confirmation that the Looney Tunes have wallowed under misuse for decades. Once the crown jewel of not only Warners IP but also American animation in general (at least this side of Disney), the Looney Tunes were passed down from each generation to the next since the 1940s as an almost timeless entertainment and crash course in physical comedy and vaudeville patter banter. There are of course exceptions (hence Peppy Le Pew’s humorous cameo in Coyote vs. Acme ), but even many of the dated elements have their charms.
